nature: EXPLORATORY numerical-sensitivity analysis, planned after the 6,600-evaluation C_Q-vs-C_Lap results were seen; not confirmatory
evaluator: laplace_k_criterion v1 via run_k_exp2_clap_comparison.evaluate_state (unchanged); N = n = 150; d_K = Kd - K(K-1)/2; grad_tol 1e-8
forbidden: choosing the better of two runs
failure_rule: status recorded once (OK / NOT_STATIONARY / HESSIAN_NOT_PD / ERROR); a dataset with any non-OK evaluation is INCOMPLETE under the rule being analysed; denominator stays 10
selection_rule: argmin_K of the 2-init unweighted mean; ties <= 1e-9 -> smaller K
question: are the C_Lap INCOMPLETE datasets due to the Newton iteration cap or to a deeper numerical instability?
targets: the 52 NOT_STATIONARY and 5 HESSIAN_NOT_PD official rows
procedure: reproduce each target with max_iter 200 (Z_last): status, grad_inf and Phi must equal the official record bitwise (STOP otherwise)
NOT_STATIONARY: evaluate ONCE with max_iter 400, Z_last, grad_tol 1e-8; record status/value
HESSIAN_NOT_PD: no rescue; record the eigen-spectrum of H at the returned point (n negative, 5 smallest)
tech_check: max_iter 400 leaves evaluations that converged within 200 iterations bitwise unchanged (smoke states + 40 official OK rows); hence the 'B rule' equals a uniform max_iter = 400 rule applied to every evaluation
analysis: INCOMPLETE datasets under the B rule vs official
exact/under/over under the B rule (reported next to, never replacing, the official counts)
selection bias: K_TRUE and C_Q-outcome mix of complete vs INCOMPLETE datasets
